status_summary: Executive Order 14268 (signed 2025-04-09) directed State and Defense to send Congress a joint letter proposing an update to the statutory arms-sale certification, or notification, thresholds (Sec. 3(a)(iii)), without stating the direction of the change, and work with it on faster notification review, to name priority partners and end-items within 60 days, to plan for exportability as an early acquisition requirement within 90 days, and to plan a single tracking system for sales cases within 120 days; it does not mention tiered review or contracting capacity by name. Executive Order 14383 (signed 2026-02-06) ordered an America First Arms Transfer Strategy, a sales task force, quarterly metrics on sales cases and licenses, and reassigned some notification functions. The Department's Acquisition Transformation Strategy (posted 2025-11-10) says a separate response to EO 14268 covers foreign military sales reform, that a root cause analysis of the worst-performing sales cases was underway, and that planned phase-two changes include exportability decisions in the milestone process and moving the Defense Security Cooperation Agency and the Defense Technology Security Administration under the operational control of the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment (ExecutiveGov reported the agency move in November 2025; CRS dates the realignment to 2026-02-10). The FY2026 NDAA (Public Law 119-60, dated 2025-12-18) lists in its table of contents Sec. 903 (Assistant Secretary of Defense for International Armaments Cooperation), Sec. 1211 (improvements to security cooperation workforce and defense acquisition workforce), Sec. 1212 (modifications to foreign military sales processes), Sec. 1213 (periodic review of FMS-only list) and Sec. 5603 (report on a processing fee for ITAR license applications); the section texts were not read. H.R. 3613, which would raise notification thresholds, was ordered reported by the House Foreign Affairs Committee on 2025-07-22; later floor action was not verified. A CRS report updated 2026-05-13 describes tiered review (20 to 40 days) without reporting any change to it, so no end to tiered review was found. CRS (version of 2026-07-27) reports that on 2026-02-10 the Department realigned the Defense Security Cooperation Agency and the Defense Technology Security Administration under the Under Secretary for Acquisition and Sustainment as a single arms-sales enterprise; it cites P.L. 119-60 Secs. 1211 to 1215 among legislation proposed or enacted to improve FMS, which it says is intended to codify parts of EO 14268, without describing each section, and it puts FY2025 FMS-system activity at 104.4 billion dollars. On 2026-05-13 the House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced further arms-sales bills, including H.R. 8665 (Allied Defense Sales Act) and a foreign military financing loan bill; the committee release mentions no change to notification thresholds or tiered review.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14268 signed (published 2025-04-15): priority partner and end-item lists within 60 days, exportability plan within 90 days, case-tracking system plan within 120 days, a joint proposal to Congress on notification thresholds, and review of the FMS-only list and the U.S. Munitions List.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee orders H.R. 3613, the Streamlining Foreign Military Sales Act of 2025, reported; the bill would raise the dollar thresholds for notifying Congress of foreign military and direct commercial sales (CBO). Later floor action was not verified.

The Department posts its Acquisition Transformation Strategy, which says a separate response to EO 14268 covers foreign military sales reform, that a root cause analysis of the worst-performing sales cases is underway, and that planned phase-two changes include exportability decisions in the milestone decision process and moving the Defense Security Cooperation Agency and the Defense Technology Security Administration under the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment. ExecutiveGov reports the Defense Secretary's changes include moving the agency from the policy office to the acquisition office.

The FY2026 NDAA becomes Public Law 119-60 (date shown on govinfo.gov). Its table of contents lists Sec. 903 (Assistant Secretary of Defense for International Armaments Cooperation), Sec. 1211 (security cooperation and defense acquisition workforce), Sec. 1212 (modifications to foreign military sales processes), Sec. 1213 (periodic review of FMS-only list) and Sec. 5603 (report on a processing fee for ITAR license applications); the section texts were not read.

Executive Order 14383, Establishing an America First Arms Transfer Strategy, signed (published 2026-02-11): a sales catalog and industry plan within 60 to 120 days, a Promoting American Military Sales Task Force within 30 days, quarterly public metrics within 120 days, and reassignment of some congressional-notification functions.

DOD realigns the Defense Security Cooperation Agency and the Defense Technology Security Administration under the Under Secretary for Acquisition and Sustainment, described as a single enterprise for arms sales (per CRS).

CRS updates its report on the arms sales congressional review process; it describes tiered review (20 to 40 days) and the statutory review periods with no reported change, and notes emergency waivers the Secretary of State invoked in March and May 2026 for sales to Israel, the UAE, Jordan, Kuwait and Qatar.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee advances arms-sales measures including H.R. 8665 (Allied Defense Sales Act, a multinational sales strategy) and a foreign military financing loan authorization bill; the release gives no notification thresholds or tiered-review changes.

title: Speed foreign military sales: end tiered review, fund contracting, plan for exportability
uncertainties: Whether tiered review has ended could not be determined: the CRS report (May 2026) repeats older descriptions and does not mention the 2025 or 2026 orders, so absence of a reported change is weak evidence. Not found: FY2025 or FY2026 foreign military sales totals, whether the joint threshold proposal was sent to Congress, the later status of H.R. 3613, the output of the 60-, 90- and 120-day plans, or any ITAR change for the UK, Canada or Australia. The DSCA move was first reported by ExecutiveGov; the NDAA assistant secretary provision comes from an Atlantic Council guide. The oversight concern in the blockers rests on a Stimson Center analysis (think tank commentary) whose author and date were not shown on the page; it is an argument, not a finding. A Nov 2025 companion arms-transfer memo is mentioned in a law-firm footnote, but its contents were not found. Searches run: one news search on notification changes and one on NDAA and bill implementation; Federal Register fetches for both orders. The Department's Acquisition Transformation Strategy (read through its first 100,000 characters) describes FMS reform as planned phases and says nothing on ITAR, tiered review or FMS contracting capacity; the Secretary's separate response to EO 14268 was not found. P.L. 119-60 was checked only through its table of contents. On recheck of 2026-10-12 the DSCA and DTSA realignment is now backed by CRS, which dates it 2026-02-10; the earlier ExecutiveGov report from November 2025 likely described the announced plan (inference). The section titles of P.L. 119-60 Secs. 1211 to 1215 were confirmed on govinfo.gov, but their text was not read, and the link to EO 14268 is CRS's statement of intent, not a finding that the sections carry out the order. No end to tiered review, enacted threshold change, or ITAR easing was found. Floor action on H.R. 3613 and H.R. 8665 was not found. FY2027 House NDAA text on FMS (Sec. 1817 on industrial-base demand, per a War on the Rocks comparison) is adjacent only. Order numbers and dates for EO 14268 (signed 2025-04-09, published 2025-04-15) and EO 14383 (signed 2026-02-06, published 2026-02-11) were confirmed through the Federal Register API and full text. Neither order uses the term tiered review or addresses contracting capacity or ITAR by name; EO 14268 Sec. 3(c)(ii) directs a review of the FMS-only list and U.S. Munitions List, Sec. 2(b) and 4(a) address parallel decision-making, and EO 14383 Sec. 4(v) amends the allocation of congressional notification functions. The law.cornell.edu page for 22 U.S.C. 2776 shows the older thresholds and a 15 and 30 day statutory review, with amendment history ending in 2014, so it is weak evidence that the statute was unchanged. The 22 U.S.C. 2778 notes record that P.L. 119-60 Sec. 1085 is the AUKUS Improvement Act of 2025, which amends that section, and show a periodic review of the Excluded Technology List; the contents of Sec. 1085 as an ITAR easing for the UK and Australia were not read. The GovInfo HTML of P.L. 119-60 returned for this pass ended in Division A Title I (Sec. 127), so Secs. 903, 1211 to 1213 and 5603 remain unread.
